HEEWON STYLE — a premium KOREAN WEBTOON / MANHWA splash illustration of a group, lit with cinematic tenebrism. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). THREE FIGURES STACKED IN DEPTH, each waist-up, the nearest largest. DRAW IT EXACTLY IN THE STYLE OF THE ATTACHED CHARACTER SHEET: the same clean confident black ink linework, the same manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair). It must read as an INKED DRAWING: visible line strokes everywhere — bold tapered contour lines around every figure, drawn fold lines in the silk and armour, hair drawn as inked strands, a little cross-hatching and line shading in the shadows — then flat cel-shading in two or three tones per colour, no airbrushed gradients. Each face must be recognisably the character drawn on the sheet, wearing the same clothes. NOT realistic, NOT an oil painting, NOT photoreal, NOT painterly, NOT a 3D render, no skin pores or photographic texture. ONLY THESE THREE PEOPLE in the frame. THREE GENERATIONS OF THE GAYA LINE, one behind the other. Furthest back, the grandfather Muryuk, old, in a tall Gaya conical helm, almost lost in the dark, a faint purple edge light (#8B5CF6) on the helm and one cheek, gazing at his son's back. In the middle, the father Seohyun, grey-streaked, stern but quietly proud, a plum key on his face, gazing at his own son's back. In front, the son Yushin, a young beardless hwarang with his crescent-moon headband, facing the camera, jaw set, a hard blue key (#2A5FB8) from the side. Each looks only at the one ahead of him; none look at each other. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. CHARACTER SHEET (copy these faces, hair and clothes exactly): LEFT of the sheet = KIM MURYUK; MIDDLE of the sheet = KIM SEOHYUN; RIGHT of the sheet = KIM YUSHIN. KIM MURYUK — Look: Square weathered Gaya face, heavy brows, long pauses in the eyes; grows grey, then white, but never bald under the helm. Dress: Out of battle: plain dark Gaya-cut po with a purple sash; his Gaya helm (rounded iron bowl, wide flared brim, tall red horsehair cone) on his head or under his arm, ALWAYS, even indoors at home (it sits on a stand by the door at night). Now: Very old: white beard, a stick, four blankets, the helm still on. Colour #8B5CF6. | KIM SEOHYUN — Look: Gentle long face, apologetic eyes, a careful mouth; a softer cousin of young Yushin's face, never the same man. Completely clean-shaven and long-haired when young (loose topknot, long strands past the jaw); a thin moustache and short beard from his forties. Now: Grey-templed provincial governor and general; Silla steel lamellar on campaign. Colour #3E8EF0. | KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Hwarang years (stage portrait): BEARDLESS, Silla-blue headband with a gold crescent moon, its tails trailing. Colour #2A5FB8. LIGHT AND BACKGROUND (deep manhwa tenebrism, darker than a normal splash page): about TWO-THIRDS OF THE FRAME IS PURE INK-BLACK. No set, no architecture or floor beyond what the scene names, no props beyond what the characters hold. Each figure is pulled out of the black by ONE hard, narrow key light from the side or from below in THAT PERSON'S OWN COLOUR, catching only a cheekbone, an eye, the bridge of the nose, the edge of a sleeve, a plate of armour or a hand; the rest of each figure falls off into solid black shadow and merges with the background, so neighbouring figures are separated only by their coloured edge light. Faces readable but half in shadow, eyes catching the light. At most a few thin wisps of smoke tinted by those coloured lights. Deep inky blacks, crisp highlights, hard cast shadows. Each person's colour is the colour of the light on them — never a glow aura, halo or outline glow. BLOCKING, BODY LANGUAGE AND FACIAL EXPRESSIONS show who they are to each other at a glance. Faces and clothes from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. One of each person, never cloned. No text, no lettering, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
